title: The Intercession of Christ
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The intercession of Christ is His ongoing ministry of representing, praying for, and preserving His people before the Father. The risen Lord lives to intercede for those who draw near to God through Him.
summary: The intercession of Christ is His ongoing ministry of representing, praying for, and preserving His people before the Father. The risen Lord lives to intercede for those who draw near to God through Him.
christFocus: Jesus intercedes as the crucified, risen, and exalted Savior. His prayers are grounded in His finished work, His righteousness, and His perfect love for His people.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Christ’s saving work did not end in abandonment of His people. The risen Lord continues His priestly ministry by interceding for them before the Father.

His intercession rests on His finished sacrifice. He does not plead excuses for sin, but represents His people on the basis of His blood, righteousness, and covenant faithfulness.

Jesus intercedes personally and effectually. He prayed for Peter before his fall, and He prayed for all who would believe through the apostles’ word. His care is not distant or general.

Because He always lives to intercede, He is able to save completely. The perseverance of believers rests not in their grip on Him, but in His faithful priestly ministry for them.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Believers often fear that weakness, failure, or spiritual attack will separate them from God. Christ’s intercession gives stronger comfort: the Savior Himself represents His people before the Father.

This doctrine also humbles pride. Christians do not continue by self-sufficiency. They are kept by the living Christ who prays for them and brings them safely through.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Rest in the intercession of Christ when you feel weak, accused, or afraid. Come to God through Him, pray with confidence, and encourage struggling believers that Jesus is not finished caring for His own.
